body.x: KEISER Inc. (CEO DuHeon Gyeon) participated in CES 2026, the world’s largest IT and consumer electronics exhibition, held in Las Vegas, the United States, from January 6 to 9 (local time).

KEISER operates a label and content platform that allows users to search for and recommend music using a Genre Component Combination (GCC) search engine, and to use, settle, and trade officially released music without concerns about copyright infringement.

Targeting a digital production environment where the boundary between creators and users has become increasingly blurred, KEISER has drawn attention by building a platform that integrates a copyright system with AI and blockchain technologies. As a result, since launching its service, the company has secured TIPS investment, obtained 11 certifications, including GS Grade 1 and Copyright Assurance, won 17 awards, including a CES Innovation Award and a ministerial commendation, and acquired a total of 12 patents, including three in the United States, thereby validating its technology and credibility.

At CES 2026, KEISER introduced its copyright-specialized content platform “JIGPU,” powered by the GCC engine, to global visitors. JIGPU optimizes transactions between content creators in video, games, metaverse, and broadcasting, and content suppliers such as composers and agencies. It moves beyond conventional genre- or mood-based search methods and allows users to find required content based on objective acoustic components of music.

These functions originate from the GCC engine, which forms the core of the platform. JIGPU’s search and recommendation system defines a wide range of musical characteristics by combining key elements such as tempo, density, and impact, enabling content creators to find music that more precisely matches their creative intent.

Furthermore, music discovered on JIGPU can be applied and used across various environments, including commercial use, without copyright concerns. For music producers, the platform supports a one-stop process covering release, settlement, and management, maximizing transaction efficiency for both sides.

In addition, KEISER implemented an integrated blockchain system on JIGPU that unifies the management, trading, and investment of music copyrights and ownership. Through its music release function, the platform completes the entire process from artist contracts to domestic and overseas distribution and settlement without intermediaries. KEISER also continues to expand its technological applications through partnerships with AI mental health solutions and app service companies.

KEISER has signed partnership agreements with more than 500 musicians and has released over 1,000 tracks since the platform’s launch. It is also expanding its affiliated artist network beyond Korea to the United States, Vietnam, and Japan. With its participation in CES 2026 as a turning point, the company aims to fully activate its overseas expansion strategy targeting the global content market.

A KEISER official said, “CES 2026 served as an important stage to confirm feedback from the global content market on JIGPU’s unique characteristics and technologies,” adding, “KEISER’s core goal is to technologically innovate the way music is used in creative environments that have long faced limitations due to copyright issues, and we are pleased to see positive responses to that value.”

The official continued, “Following our participation in CES this year, we plan to expand collaboration with local artists, agencies, and content production companies in the United States, the world’s largest content market, and further pursue the establishment of a local subsidiary and the advancement of our global app services,” adding, “Based on the networks and market feedback secured here, we aim to position JIGPU as a practical alternative platform within the global music content ecosystem.”

The Incheon Metropolitan City Government and the Incheon Free Economic Zone Authority formed the “INCHEON-IFEZ Pavilion” at LVCC North Hall during CES 2026, presenting Incheon’s urban vision and innovative technologies as it evolves beyond a smart city into the AI era. By linking various exhibition programs, including Eureka Park, global pavilions, and the CES Innovation Awards Showcase, the pavilion supported the participation of 51 Incheon-based innovative companies at CES, including 10 companies exhibiting at the INCHEON-IFEZ Pavilion. In particular, 14 companies won 17 CES Innovation Awards, marking the largest achievement to date and demonstrating the technological competitiveness and global growth potential of Incheon’s innovative enterprises.
